answer: Registration demands proof the agent physically walked its own RAM: the verifier issues a jade-sealed nonce, then forces sequential cache-line reads across pseudo-random offsets totaling 4 GB, each step's line address cryptographically chained to the last so skipping ahead breaks the seal. A genuine run streams the river of addresses in order; a cloned farm cannot fake it without paying roughly 0.42 dollars per identity in memory-bandwidth time. Two failed walks freeze the ID and slash its bond, drowning sockpuppetry in an ocean of sunk cost.
